1._section_summary: This abstract describes a two-study investigation of the relationship between appearance goals for exercise and body image. Study 1 (n=215 female UK students, ages 17-30) used a cross-sectional design to examine how appearance goals indirectly negatively associate with body image through introjected (guilt-based) exercise regulation. Study 2 (n=165, ages 18-27) experimentally manipulated guilt and appearance goals to test whether guilt increases body anxiety, finding that guilt manipulation significantly increased post-test guilt and body anxiety among participants in the guilt condition.

Study 1 is a cross-sectional study using structural equation modeling to test direct and indirect associations between these variables. Study 2 is an experimental study with a 2 × 2 design that manipulates guilt related to exercise and appearance goals orthogonally to test the proposed mediation process. The research focuses on women due to documented body image concerns in this population and differential effects of exercise on body image by gender.

1._section_summary: This section describes the post-test and trait measures used in an experimental study examining the effects of guilt and appearance/health-focused article exposure on body anxiety and exercise motivation. Post-test measures included questions about the article, guilt and negative emotion (I-PANAS-SF), body anxiety (PASTAS), and exercise regulation (BREQ-2), with demographic information and self-reported height/weight collected for BMI calculation. Two weeks later, participants completed trait measures of body anxiety, exercise goals (GCEQ), and introjected regulation via an online survey (n = 130).
